categoryReasons.schemaAndBindings: The pokemon and detail request IDs align with data.pokemon and params.name, and the filter, selection, and direct lookup controls all provide bound defaults.
categoryReasons.apiAndRequestDesign: The source and list/detail GET routes match the verified PokéAPI paths, and the detail request uses the required manual name parameter.
categoryReasons.runtimeCompatibility: The JSX uses supported components and collection expressions, a literal SubFetch ID, safe number formatting, and no reserved callback names.
categoryReasons.goalFulfillment: The responsive browse/detail layout includes direct lookup, a filtered loaded list, official artwork and game sprite, types, abilities, and stat bars, though the list-state branches are inconsistent.
categoryReasons.visualQuality: Artwork, type badges, labeled measurements, and stat bars create useful Pokémon-specific hierarchy, while the text-only names and duplicate status messages add clutter.
categoryReasons.responsiveAndTheme: The auto-fit SimpleGrids use flexible minimum widths, the list has no fixed height, and the palette is expressed through theme-compatible component colors.
categoryReasons.loadingEmptyErrorSuccess: The template provides list loading, failure, empty, initial, and success states plus SubFetch-managed detail states, but the pre-data branch can show an empty message alongside the initial message and empty/failure feedback is duplicated.
categoryReasons.dailyUsefulness: Direct lookup, local filtering, searchable selection, and a persistent detail column are useful, but users must select names separately from the inert text list and the list-state messages can conflict.
categoryReasons.complexityDiscipline: The request design is compact and repeated filter expressions support counts and rendered content, but list loading, empty, failure, and initial messages are duplicated across branches.
categoryReasons.accessibility: The inputs and selector have labels, detail launch has an aria label, both sprites have alt text, and status feedback is textual.
categoryReasons.actionSafety: The widget contains only read-only GET requests and no mutating action.

strengths: Direct and selected lookup share one correctly parameterized manual detail request.
A responsive split layout keeps the loaded list and details separate.
Detail output covers sprites, types, abilities, measurements, and base stats.
The widget uses flexible sizing, explicit control labels, and read-only requests.
problems: Before list data is available, the left-column empty branch can display 'No Pokémon names were returned' at the same time as the initial 'will appear here once loaded' message.
Empty and failure feedback is emitted in both the browse section and the footer state branches.
The visible filtered names are inert text, while selection happens in a separate searchable Select.
highestImpactFixes: Gate the empty state on a successful list response and consolidate list status rendering so only one state message appears.
Remove the duplicate empty and failure messages while preserving the visible initial, loading, and retry states.
Align the visible filtered names with the existing Select workflow or remove the redundant inert list.
